meta_analysis: Bowes, Costello & Tasimi (2023) — The Conspiratorial Mind: motivational and personological correlates of conspiratorial ideation
rationale: Bowes is a CORRELATES meta-analysis: each effect size is a zero-order correlation r between conspiratorial ideation and a psychological construct, nested article -> study -> SAMPLE -> effect-size. We replicate EXACTLY the variables Jansen 2025 benchmarked (no extras): study-level YearOfPub, CTType, COVID, Outcome; sample-level Females and Sample(recruitment); and the effect-size triple outcome/es/N (phase 2). KEY granularity decision: studies ~= articles (169 studies / 165 articles, multi-study rare) but SAMPLES are frequently multiple (257 samples / 169 studies; e.g. Betsch2018 = 1 study, 2 samples). So Females, recruitment and N are SAMPLE-scoped (each sample has its own), unlike Jansen who collapsed to one-per-paper. CRITICAL FIX: gold `Females` is a PERCENTAGE (0-100, mean 56.95), not an absolute count — Jansen extracted counts and scored 0.03; we extract female_pct to match gold. Gold lives in RDataFile2023Final.xlsx 'For R' sheet.

fields.name: Sample
fields.definition: Anchors the within-paper sample census. Each distinct participant SAMPLE the paper reports correlations for is one record. Most papers have ONE sample -> sample_key 'main sample'. A paper that reports SEPARATE samples / studies / data collections with their own N and their own correlation set emits one record per sample -> 'Study 1', 'Study 2' (or 'Sample 1', 'Sample 2'). DO NOT put author/year in the sample_key. total_n is this sample's overall N (the denominator the correlations are based on). The Females / Sample-recruitment values and the effect sizes key off these same sample labels. YearOfPub / CTType / COVID / Outcome are study-level (shared across the paper's samples).

fields.name: YearOfPub
fields.definition: Official year of publication of the article (format XXXX). Not the submission/acceptance/online-posting year unless that is the only date available.
fields.skill_hints: Look at the study header, citation/copyright line, or any year on the first page ('published', 'online', copyright year). One value per paper.

fields.name: CTType

value_labels.General: General belief in conspiracy theories with no focus on specific events/narratives (e.g. generic conspiracist-belief scales).
value_labels.Specific: Concrete, event-based conspiracy theories (e.g. 9/11 was an inside job, faked moon landing).
value_labels.Stereotype: Conspiracy beliefs tied to outgroup stereotypes (e.g. a group conspiring for dominance).
value_labels.Scenario: Hypothetical/scenario-based conspiracies where participants read a conspiratorial scenario.
value_labels.Fictitious: Conspiracy theories that are not publicly circulated (invented for the study, e.g. Red Bull is carcinogenic and hidden).
value_labels.Mix: Combines different conspiracy types, or does not differentiate specific vs general.

fields.definition: Type of conspiracy theory the study's conspiratorial-ideation measure assessed. Multi-label only when the study genuinely uses more than one distinct type; otherwise a single token. Map to 'Mix' when types are combined / undifferentiated.
fields.skill_hints: Read the conspiracy-belief MEASURE described in Methods/Materials. Generic Conspiracist Beliefs Scale / Conspiracy Mentality -> General. Named real events -> Specific. Invented item -> Fictitious. Scenario vignette -> Scenario. Outgroup-stereotype items -> Stereotype.

fields.name: Females
fields.comment_on_gender: IS the gender metric, expressed as PERCENT female of the sample (gold convention), NOT decomposed [total,female,male] and NOT an absolute count.
fields.definition: Percentage of THIS sample that is female (0-100). Bowes gold stores female PERCENT, so report a percentage even if the paper gives a raw count: female_pct = (n_female / N) * 100. If only n_male is given, female_pct = (N - n_male)/N * 100. All-female -> 100; all-male -> 0. One value per SAMPLE (a paper with two samples has two female% values).
fields.skill_hints: Find the Participants/Sample demographics for EACH sample. Keywords: 'female', 'women', 'male', 'men', '% female', 'gender'. Convert any count to a percentage of that sample's N. Do NOT report the absolute number.

fields.name: SampleType

value_labels.Com: Community / general public / online panel (e.g. MTurk, Prolific, general adult sample).
value_labels.Mixed: Composed of participants from more than one category (e.g. students AND community).
value_labels.Soldier: Military personnel, serving or with a military background.

fields.definition: Recruitment category of THIS sample (Jansen variable 'Sample'). One value per sample. Use 'Mixed' when a single sample combines multiple recruitment sources; use 'Com' for general-public / online-panel adults.
fields.skill_hints: Read recruitment text in Methods/Participants. 'undergraduates / psychology students' -> Student. 'MTurk / Prolific / online panel / general public / community adults' -> Com. 'students and community' in one sample -> Mixed. 'soldiers / military / veterans' -> Soldier.

fields.name: COVID

value_labels.Yes: The conspiracy measure specifically assessed COVID-19 conspiracy theories.
value_labels.No: The measure did not specifically assess COVID-19 conspiracy theories.

fields.definition: Whether the study specifically assessed COVID-19 conspiracy theories. 'Yes' only if the conspiratorial-ideation measure is explicitly about COVID-19/pandemic conspiracies; otherwise 'No'.
fields.skill_hints: Look at the conspiracy measure / Materials. Keywords: 'COVID-19', 'coronavirus', 'pandemic'. A general conspiracy scale that happens to be administered during 2020-2022 is still 'No' unless its ITEMS are COVID-specific.

fields.name: Outcome
fields.definition: The set of psychological/behavioral constructs the study correlated with conspiratorial ideation, each mapped to its controlled-vocabulary token. Multi-label: list every construct measured. Map a measured construct to a token ONLY when it clearly matches; skip constructs with no token. This is the study-level union of the per-effect-size `outcome` values.
fields.skill_hints: Read Methods (Measures) and the correlation table headers/results. Each scale that is correlated with the conspiracy measure -> its token (e.g. Big Five NEO -> Neuro/Extra/Open/Agree/Consc; RWA scale -> RWA; paranoia scale -> Paranoia). Use the correlation matrix as the authoritative list of measured constructs.
